summary: Chamcha Market is a small weekend craft market in the Loang Him Kao community east of Chiang Mai. Recent stall signs confirm drop-in wood painting at Awila Handicraft (75/95/159 baht by item size) and an Art & Workshops stall offering watercolour, drawing and ceramics. Treat this as a choice of maker-run activities on the day, rather than a single scheduled class.
whyGo: Try a short, affordable hands-on activity among working local makers, then browse crafts and food beneath the rain trees.
The market is part of Loang Him Kao, a craft and arts community with cafés and independent shops along its lanes.
bestFor: Casual makers who are happy to choose from whatever stalls are operating that weekend.
Pairing a simple craft activity with a relaxed market visit and local snacks.
skipIf: You need a guaranteed class, English-language instruction, a specific medium or a fixed duration; these details are not published for the market stalls.
You cannot visit on Saturday or Sunday, when Chamcha Market operates.
duration: Allow about 1–2 hours for browsing and a simple activity; this is a planning estimate, since stall-specific class durations are not published.
cost: A field report transcribing stall signs on 27 September 2026 lists wood-painting at Awila Handicraft for 75, 95 or 159 baht depending on item size. Prices for watercolour, drawing and ceramics were not stated; confirm at the stall. No general market admission charge was identified.
hours: Saturday and Sunday. The Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT) lists 09:00–14:30; a local field report records the market banner as 09:00–15:00. Arrive earlier in the day and check the market's Facebook page for changes.
bestTime: Go in the morning, when the market is open and you have more time to find an available workshop before stalls close.
gettingThere: The market is at 13, 16 Moo 2 Soi 11, San Klang, San Kamphaeng, Chiang Mai 50130. TAT estimates about 20 minutes by car from Chiang Mai Old City; its Loang Him Kao page says about 25 minutes east from Tha Phae Gate. These are estimates and traffic dependent. A taxi or ride-hail car is the practical option; parking is reported nearby, but confirm availability. Search maps for Chamcha Market rather than Loang Him Kao Village.
booking: No advance booking process is listed for these market stalls. Ask at Awila Handicraft or the Art & Workshops stall on arrival; contact Chamcha Market at 097-462-4296 or check facebook.com/ChamchaMarket for current market information. Availability, language and whether ceramics need a later collection are unconfirmed.
accessibility: This is an open-air market with lanes between stalls; step-free routes, accessible toilets and seating at the workshop stalls are not documented. Contact the market before travelling if you need step-free access or specific facilities.
practicalTips: Check the Chamcha Market Facebook page close to your visit: the market is weekend-only and the workshop makers or activities may vary.
Bring cash in small denominations for a low-cost stall activity and market purchases.
Ask the maker to confirm the full price, how long the activity takes and whether a ceramic piece is ready to take away or needs firing and later collection.
decemberNotes: December 2026 workshop rosters and holiday operating changes have not been published in the sources checked. The regular weekend market is the best current expectation, but confirm dates and workshop availability shortly before visiting. Chiang Mai's cool season can make a morning outdoors pleasant; the market is still open-air.
uncertainties: No dated schedule for December 2026, workshop roster, reservation requirement, class duration, language, or ceramic firing and collection details was found.
TAT lists closing at 14:30, while the local field report transcribed the market banner as 15:00.
The 27 September 2026 field report is current and specific but is not the market operator; workshop prices and stall participation can change.
